question.text: Stock P has sigma 20%, Stock Q has sigma 10%. Correlation = 0.5. Equal-weighted, portfolio standard deviation (approx) is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Var = 0.25*0.04 + 0.25*0.01 + 2*0.5*0.5*0.5*0.2*0.1 = 0.01 + 0.0025 + 0.005 = 0.0175; sigma = sqrt(0.0175) ~ 13.23%. The Trap: Simple average (15%) ignores correlation benefit. Cross-Exam Context: Same formula used in X-A, XV. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Show clients the diversification benefit numerically — it builds trust in the PM process.
